replacements.old:
Children's life insurance: what it does and when it makes sense

A child's life insurance policy is small whole life coverage that a parent or grandparent buys and the child keeps as an adult. It is not for everyone. Here is what it does, and the cheaper alternative many families overlook.
replacements.new:
Children's & juvenile life insurance: a child policy or a child rider?

Children's life insurance, also called juvenile life insurance, is usually a small whole life policy that a parent or grandparent buys on a child or grandchild. The child can keep it as an adult. It is not for everyone. Here is what it does, and how it compares with a child rider on a parent's policy. We price both side by side.
replacements.why: Plan item 9: H1 names juvenile life insurance and the policy-or-rider choice; 'grandchild' in the first paragraph; 'the cheaper alternative' (unsourced price claim) becomes 'we price both side by side'.

replacements.old:
• Locks in insurability. The child has coverage for life at the price set today, whatever health conditions appear later. Many policies include the right to buy more coverage at set ages without health questions.
  • Fixed premiums. The premium is set by the child's age at purchase and does not rise.
replacements.new:
• Locks in insurability. As long as premiums are paid, the coverage stays in force even if health conditions appear later. Many policies include the right to buy more coverage at set ages without health questions.
  • Usually level premiums. The premium is set by the child's age at purchase. On many policies it stays level, but terms vary, so check the policy.
replacements.why: Hedge the certainty wording: 'does not rise' and 'coverage for life at the price set today' become level on most policies, check the policy (same approach as the final expense fix). Checker: 'most policies' removed (banned word 'most', and an unsourced share).

replacements.old: A whole life policy on a child has a death benefit and a cash value account. A portion of each premium goes to insurance costs and fees, and the rest builds cash value, which grows at a guaranteed rate and may also earn dividends if the policy is from a mutual company. In the early years, cash value is usually small, then builds more noticeably over the long term.
replacements.new: A whole life policy on a child has a death benefit and a cash value. The cash value is part of the insurance policy. It is not a separate savings account. A portion of each premium goes to insurance costs and fees, and the rest builds the policy's guaranteed cash value. Some policies from mutual companies may also pay dividends, which are not guaranteed. In the early years, cash value is usually small, then builds more noticeably over the long term.
replacements.why: 'A cash value account' presents the policy as an account; reworded so cash value is part of the policy, not a savings account (14VAC5-41-30(E), 41-70(L)). Dividends now say 'not guaranteed' (14VAC5-41-60(D)). Checker: smoother wording; TDI life guide added ('Dividends aren't guaranteed').
sources: https://www.tdi.texas.gov/pubs/consumer/cb018.html (Texas Department of Insurance, Life insurance guide, last updated Dec 12, 2025)
